**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat whitespace-only ControlSource as unbound**

When a control has `ControlSource = " "`, the runtime treats it as unbound elsewhere because `write_native_list_control_controlsource_target` trims the value before checking emptiness, but this guard requires the raw string to be empty. Such a control therefore falls through to the legacy `std::llround` path: for example, `RemoveItem(2.9)` removes row 3 instead of the newly specified truncation to row 2, while `RemoveItem(0)` silently returns instead of raising error 11. Use the same trimmed-empty test as the binding code so all effectively unbound controls receive the checked admission behavior.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Treat exact-zero RowSourceType as the default**

When `RowSourceType` is assigned an exact zero such as `CAST(0 AS INT64)` or `CAST(0 AS UINT64)`, the generic property writer preserves that value kind, while `native_list_control_rowsourcetype_supports_additem()` already treats it as row-source type 0 via `value_as_number()`. This stricter `kind == number` check therefore bypasses the new checked path: on an otherwise unbound control, `RemoveItem(2.9)` falls back to `llround` and removes row 3 rather than truncating to row 2, and invalid values retain the legacy silent behavior. Test the numeric value as zero, as the analogous TopIndex/TopItemID guards do, rather than requiring the double-backed kind.
